definition: Sparse means thinly scattered or spread out, with wide gaps in between — not dense or crowded.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sparse. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sparse should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: His notes for the exam were sparse: a few scattered phrases on an otherwise empty page.
"Thin" is milder than sparse — a thin crowd still fills most of the space, just loosely.
"Barren" is stronger than sparse — a sparse field has a little growing here and there, but a barren field has almost nothing at all.

Scattered means spread thinly here and there over an area — scattered showers, scattered applause. It describes where the few things sit. Sparse describes the overall density that results: so few, so far apart, that the space feels empty. Scattered points at the dots; sparse measures the gaps.

Patchy means uneven — thick in some spots and completely missing in others, like patchy fog or a patchy beard. Sparse is thin everywhere, evenly short of coverage. A sparse lawn is thin across the whole yard; a patchy one is lush here and bald there.

Dispersed means spread out over a wide area, often after being deliberately broken up — a crowd dispersed by police, seeds dispersed by wind. It is about the spreading. Sparse is about the result being thin: wide gaps, little coverage. A dispersed crowd went elsewhere; a sparse crowd never filled the room.

A desert's plants are sparse (spread thin); its water is scarce (not enough to go around).

Over the city, the night sky is sparse — a dozen faint stars, wide fields of blank black between them, the whole dome thinned to almost nothing.
